subject: SLA-driven SKU allocation plan for Dedicated (NovaAI POC)
messages:
From: Simon Cho <simon.cho@novumai.com>
To: aisha.rahman@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com
Cc: ops@novumai.com
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity — initial sizing for NovaAI POC

Hi Aisha / Dev,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We want to run a six-week POC on Redwood Dedicated to validate latency and cost for our multimodal assistant. High-level constraints:
- SLA: 99.9% availability, 95th pct latency < 180ms for typical 256-token responses
- Workload: mixed; 60% short chat (<=128 tokens), 30% mid (128-512), 10% long generation (512-2k) with occasional KV-cache heavy sessions
- Models: 1x 30B decoder + 1x 220B decoder for high-fidelity answers (we can quantize), and an embedding model for similarity lookups.
- Budget: target POC run-rate <$15k/mo; willing to trade a bit for predictable latency.

Can you propose an initial SKU allocation (H100/A100/L4 mix) with fallback plan and what telemetry/traces you need from us? Also want to know how cache affinity and single-tenant nodes affect cost/latency.

Simon
Head of Infrastructure
NovaAI

From: aisha.rahman@redwood.com <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
To: Simon Cho <simon.cho@novumai.com>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 12:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial sizing for NovaAI POC

Simon — thanks, this is helpful. High level answer up front: for your mix and SLA I recommend a hybrid pool dominated by H100s for the 220B runs, A100s for most 30B throughput, and a small L4 pool for low-cost embedding/short-chat path and risk-managed burst. Key reasons: H100s give the memory headroom for 220B without excessive sequence chopping; A100s provide better cost per throughput for quantized 30B; L4s are very cost-effective for embeddings and very short responses but struggle with long-seq KV-cache pressure.

What I'll do next: Dev will drop a short tech note with numbers (memory footprint, expected qps per GPU, batch sizes, estimated $/hour). Marissa will prepare an ops playbook for node affinity, cache warm-up, and autoscale guardrails (canary scaling, graceful fallback). To proceed we need:
- A 48-72 hour representative trace (tokens/sec by request, sequence length distribution, cold vs warm sessions)
- Top 5 longest prompt templates and average context size
- Target concurrency per customer (if multi-tenant) or single-tenant needs

I'll attach a first-pass SKU matrix and a mutual action plan for sign-off.

Best,
Aisha
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial sizing for NovaAI POC

Simon — attaching a short tech note (dedicated_sku_matrix_q3.pdf) and a sample CSV trace template (novaai_workload_sample_v1.csv). Key numbers and assumptions below. If you can share the trace with the columns in the CSV, I can run a quick sizing sim.

Assumptions: average token gen cost and latency modeled on our internal bench for similar 30B/220B decoders. Sequence-length dependent perf; quantized 8-bit for 30B, 3-bit/4-bit mixed for 220B. Memory overhead includes KV cache (runtime) + model weights + service processes.

SKU summary (approx):
- H100 (80GB): best for 220B; supports 1-2 concurrent 220B streams at 512-1k seq w/ KV cache if we accept lower batching. Estimated peak qps: 4-8 tokens/sec per GPU for long sessions; memory headroom ~20-30GB for KV cache at 1k context. Cost: high $/hr but necessary to avoid context-chopping.
- A100 (40GB/80GB variants): sweet spot for 30B quantized. At 40GB, can run multiple 30B instances with batching for higher throughput. Estimated qps: 60-160 tokens/sec per GPU for short/mid sequences when batching aggressively. Memory headroom for KV: 8-16GB depending on batch sizes. Cost: mid $/hr.
- L4 (24GB): L4 shines for embeddings and sub-128 token chat; very low cost and latency for small seqs. Not suitable for heavy KV cache or >512 seqs without chopping. Estimated qps: 200+ tokens/sec for short responses and embeddings.

Operational notes:
- Cache affinity: pin hot users/sessions to the same Dedicated node pool to keep KV caches warm; this reduces tail latency but increases fragmentation. We recommend reserving 10-20% of capacity as hot-affinity slots.
- Autoscale: prefer predictive autoscale + burst queue to avoid cold start spikes; can set a strict cost cap for the POC.
- Fallbacks: primary route -> H100/A100 pool depending on model; fallback route -> quantized A100 or L4 for degraded-accuracy but better latency. Configure automatic model variant fallback with request-level SLO annotations.

Preliminary allocation for POC (subject to trace sim):
- 2x H100 (80GB) dedicated nodes (primary for 220B)
- 6x A100 (40GB) nodes (serve 30B traffic and act as burst for 220B via quantized variants)
- 4x L4 nodes (embedding + low-cost short-chat and warm-cold buffer)

Estimated POC run-rate: ~$10k-$16k/mo depending on utilization and burst patterns. If your 220B usage is sporadic, we can reduce H100 to 1 and rely on A100 fallback for non-critical paths.

I'll run a sim once you upload traces to the S3 link you referenced.

Dev
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: dedicated_sku_matrix_q3.pdf, novaai_workload_sample_v1.csv

Thanks — that aligns with our instincts. A few clarifications before we upload traces:
- Our 220B runs are expected to be ~15% of total token volume but drive 70% of perceived latency risk. Those are often long-context (avg 900 tokens) but occur from a small set of users (power analysts).
- Most customers will be multi-tenant; concurrency per org typically 10-40 concurrent sessions.
- We will upload a 72h trace to the S3 link; filename trace-202707.zip. It includes per-request seq lengths, model_id, tenant_id, and timestamps.

1) Can you sketch what a cost vs latency curve looks like if we reduce H100 to 1 node and lean on A100 fallback for non-priority traffic?
2) What operational playbook should we hand to our on-call to respond to cache-thaw caused tail latency?

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial sizing for NovaAI POC

Simon — looping in an ops playbook and a mutual action plan (mutual_action_plan_novaai.xlsx). High level answers to your two asks:

1) Cost vs latency sketch (summary):
- Baseline (2x H100 + 6x A100 + 4x L4): expected 95th pct latency ~140-160ms; estimated $/mo midpoint $13k at 60% utilization.
- Minimal H100 (1x H100 + 6x A100 + 4x L4): 95th pct latency for 220B degrades to ~220-300ms unless we aggressively quantize or limit concurrency; cost drops ~12-18%.
- No H100 (A100-only): significant context-chop for 220B; perceived latency for power-users improves only if we accept lower answer fidelity; cost drops ~30% but risk unacceptable UX for analysts.

Recommendation: run POC with 2 H100 for the first 2 weeks, monitor tail latency and warm-cache hit rate, then evaluate dropping to 1 H100 if 220B hits are lower than projected. We can also add a soft-limit route that redirects non-critical 220B calls to quantized A100 after a short queue wait.

2) On-call playbook highlights:
- Detection: alert when 95th pct latency for model=220B > 200ms for 10m and cold-hit ratio > 25%.
- Immediate action: increase H100 pool by 1 (if reserved burst available) or temporarily reduce non-critical batch sizes on A100 to free memory for KV.
- Medium-term: kick an automated cache re-warm job for top 100 tenants and increase hot-affinity slots to 20% for 1h.
- Communication: post a status to your ops Slack channel and optionally enable degraded-mode fallback to quantized variants for affected tenants.

Next steps: we will run the trace sim and share a sensitivity report (by end of week) and a sign-off-ready mutual action plan. Can we schedule a 30-min ops/runbook review on Tues 8/16?

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
